picks.matchup: Patrick Mahomes — Passing Yards O/U 259.5 (Chiefs vs Colts)
reasoning: Mahomes threw for 352 yards in his most recent meeting with the Colts and combined for 583 yards across his two prior games against them — a strong track record vs this specific opponent.
Colts' defense just allowed Lamar Jackson to throw for 324 yards in Week 1, an early red flag for their pass coverage even though Jackson isn't a high-volume passer by trade.

Counterpoint: Mahomes threw for only 184 yards in Week 1 vs Denver, but that came in a comfortable blowout with a run-heavy second half (he also ran for a TD) — game script, not a talent or arm decline.

picks.matchup: Puka Nacua — Receiving Yards O/U 79.5 (Rams vs Giants)
reasoning: Nacua's career per-game average is 95.3 receiving yards, comfortably above this line.
An analytics projection model has him at roughly 90 receiving yards specifically for this Week 2 matchup vs the Giants.

He was quiet in Week 1 (74 yards) during the Rams' lopsided loss to San Francisco, but that came in a blowout script that likely suppressed pass volume — a more balanced game vs the Giants should mean more targets.

Colts' defense ranked 29th in the NFL in EPA/play after Week 1 and was torched for 41 points by Baltimore, a real red flag against a Chiefs offense with a history of big output vs Indy (352 passing yards from Mahomes in their last meeting).
Counterweight: Chiefs' defense was elite in Week 1 (No. 1 EPA/play, No. 2 success rate in the league), which could cap Colts' scoring and shorten the game via a likely running clock in a blowout.

Set our own total at 47.5 — below the raw sum of each team's Week 1 output (31 + 23 = 54) to account for that defensive counterweight, while still leaning Over given how leaky the Colts' defense looked.

picks.matchup: San Francisco Giants vs Los Angeles Dodgers
reasoning: The Giants are 63-89 this season, one of the worst records in MLB, while the Dodgers hold a comfortable division lead.

Kept at 72% rather than higher — a single MLB game is one of the most upset-prone units in sports (one bad outing from a starter swings it), so even a huge season-long gap in team quality doesn't make one game close to certain.

picks.matchup: 3-Leg Parlay: Man City ML + 49ers ML + Dodgers ML
reasoning: Legs: Manchester City to beat Sunderland (our estimate 78%), San Francisco 49ers to beat Miami (83%), Los Angeles Dodgers to beat San Francisco Giants (72%) — three independent games, no shared outcome dependency.

Combined hit probability is the product of the three: 0.78 x 0.83 x 0.72 = ~47%, not the 78-83% any single leg looks like on its own. Stacking strong favorites into a parlay erodes back toward a coin flip fast.

This is exactly why the unit size here is a fraction of what any single leg would get on its own (1.25-1.75 units solo vs 0.25 units combined) — the parlay is a much riskier bet than 'three safe picks' intuitively feels like.

Only 'Hits' is a real, placeable bet — a sportsbook doesn't sell 'this exact parlay misses' as a ticket, so the 'Doesn't Hit' side shown here is for probability context only, not something to stake money on.
None of the three legs is a certainty on its own (see their individual entries) — treat this as a long-shot-payout play, not a 'safe' bet.
